findings.F1: Sunday's own 24-hour return, read at Monday 00:00 UTC, is reversed over the next 48 hours (slope −0.135 per usual 24-hour move, t −4.70, 2,028 cases); on the other weekdays the same last-24-hour return predicts almost nothing over 48 hours (slopes −0.035 to +0.023, t −1.74 to +1.11).
findings.F2: The Sunday reversal is graded and widespread: by quintile of Sunday's return, the next 48 hours go from +0.165 to −0.179 usual 48-hour moves; the slope is negative for all six coins (XMR −0.258 t −3.57, XRP −0.171 t −2.24, LTC −0.143 t −2.20, BTC −0.063 t −0.93) and in 7 of 8 years (2023 the exception, +0.107 t 1.32).
findings.F3: Saturday's 24-hour return continues over the 48 hours from Monday 00:00 (slope +0.208, t 4.60, 1,789 cases), while the whole weekend's 48-hour return predicts nothing (−0.023, t −0.70). The two halves cancel, so the tested idea's whole-weekend signal is weak.
findings.F4: The Saturday continuation is less steady than the Sunday reversal: it shows in 4 of 6 coins (t 2.27 to 2.75; LTC and ZEC near 0) and in 5 of 8 years (t 2.7 to 5.0), but 2018, 2021 and 2025 are negative (t −0.36 to −1.45).
findings.F5: When a coin's 168-hour realised volatility is in its top quintile, its 24-hour return is reversed over the next 24 hours (slope −0.175, t −11.3, 3,248 cases); in the four lower quintiles the slope is −0.015 to +0.034 (t ≤ 1.7).
findings.F6: The high-volatility 24-hour reversal holds in all six coins (slopes −0.103 to −0.216, t −2.7 to −5.6) and in 7 of 8 years (strongest 2021: −0.262, t −8.3). It is weak in 2023 (44 cases) and 2024 (t −0.58).
findings.F7: The tested idea's gradation shows only at the top: weekends in the top tercile of volatility ratio continue by +0.109 usual 48-hour moves (t 2.23, 596 cases), against −0.037 (t −0.91) in the bottom tercile. This matches the inconclusive verdict (t 1.95).
findings.F8: The book's gains and risks sit on Monday and Tuesday: mean daily return 0.00135 and 0.00075, against −0.00015 to +0.00011 on the other days. 170 of its 176 top-1 % days and 170 of its 174 bottom-1 % days fall on those two days, and the top-1 % days sum to 12.49 against a total of 4.91.
findings.F9: Hours 21:00 and 22:00 UTC rise more than usual (mean +0.048 and +0.039 hourly standard deviations, t 6.18 and 5.31). This holds in all six coins (t 2.6 to 4.0), every weekday and 7 of 8 years. At about 0.04 of an hour's move per hour it is far below the 0.19 % cost of a trade, and it is not graded, so no idea is drawn from it.

ideas.idea: A coin's return over Sunday (Sunday 00:00 to Monday 00:00 UTC) is partly reversed over the next 2 days. The larger Sunday's move in either direction, the larger the opposite move over Monday and Tuesday.
ideas.consequence: A trader should fade a coin's Sunday move at Monday's open for two days, more so the larger that move, and refuse to follow it.
ideas.name: Sunday moves reverse early-week

ideas.idea: When a coin's hourly volatility over the past 7 days is high, its 24-hour return is partly reversed over the next 24 hours. The reversal is larger the larger that return and the higher that volatility.
ideas.consequence: In turbulent markets a trader should lean against the coin's last day's move for one day rather than follow it, more so the larger the move.
ideas.name: Turbulent daily moves reverse

ideas.idea: A coin's return over Saturday (Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 00:00 UTC) continues in the same direction over the 2 days after Monday 00:00 UTC. The continuation is larger the larger Saturday's move.
ideas.consequence: A trader may follow Saturday's direction over Monday and Tuesday, sized by how large Saturday's move was, while treating Sunday's move separately.
ideas.name: Saturday moves carry into week
